"You are an expert game developer. Recreate the 2007 Digital Chocolate Java ME game \"Kamikaze Robots\" as accurately as possible as a modern desktop/web game.

TECH STACK
- Prefer Godot 4 (GDScript) or HTML5 Canvas + TypeScript/Phaser, or pure Java with LibGDX if you prefer. Choose one and stick to it. Make it immediately playable (desktop window or browser).
- Keep the original low-res, cute, cartoon mobile aesthetic (pixel-art or simple vector with chunky outlines). Target \~320×480 or 480×320 portrait/landscape side-view.

CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP (must match original feel)
1. Race starts with the player robot perched at the top of a jagged/bumpy downhill slope. A large mechanical foot animates and kicks it.
2. While airborne the robot automatically spins clockwise at a rate influenced by the Spin stat.
3. Single-button control: hold the button (or hold mouse/touch) to reverse/brake the spin and orient the feet downward. Release to spin freely. Timing is everything.
4. Physics:
   - More free spin before landing = higher speed and longer/more powerful bounce.
   - Landing cleanly on both feet = strong upward/forward bounce and minimal damage.
   - Landing on one foot, arms, body, or head = reduced bounce + damage.
5. Damage system (critical):
   - Limbs detach progressively: arms first, then legs.
   - Visual: parts fly off with physics and can bounce around.
   - When only torso + head remain, the next impact can eject the head forward with an explosion trail (distance controlled by Explosion stat). If the head crosses the finish line you still win.
   - If the robot fully explodes before the finish, the race is lost.
6. Camera follows the robot smoothly. Show distance traveled (meters) at the top like the original.
7. AI opponents (1–3) race the same course. They appear as full robots or distinct shadows. They never fall apart as badly as the player.

PROGRESSION @COMMENT_BODY@ CHIPS
- Tournament mode with 25–30 levels of increasing length, steepness, and obstacle density (bumps, gaps, steeper sections).
- After every race award up to 4 chips:
  - Finish 1st
  - Achieve a required number of spins in a single jump
  - Reach a minimum jump height
  - Cover a certain distance
- Between races open an upgrade screen. Spend chips on four stats (each level has visible effect):
  - Jump (bounce height/power)
  - Spin (base rotation speed)
  - Stamina (damage resistance / how many bad landings before limbs fall)
  - Explosion (head launch distance and speed)
- Allow replaying any previously cleared level to farm missing chips.
- Optional: cosmetic body upgrades at chip thresholds (different robot skins).

MODES
- Tournament (main progression).
- Quick Race / Practice (any unlocked level, vs AI or solo).
- Simple local multiplayer (pass-and-play: up to 3 humans take turns, or simultaneous if easy).

VISUAL @COMMENT_BODY@ AUDIO STYLE
- Cute round robots with big expressive eyes, spring-loaded feet, and detachable limbs.
- Colorful cartoon hills, some levels with space/planet backgrounds matching classic screenshots.
- Particles for sparks, limb detachment, and the flaming head comet.
- Upbeat, silly chiptune/MIDI-style music and punchy SFX (kick, bounce, metal hit, explosion).

UI
- Distance meter at top.
- Chip progress indicators during race.
- Clean upgrade screen with four bars/sliders.
- Simple menu: Tournament, Quick Race, Upgrades, Settings.

IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
- Deliver a complete, runnable project with clear instructions how to build/run.
- Make physics feel snappy and readable (original was praised for good physics).
- Include at least 8–10 hand-crafted levels of rising difficulty (procedural is fine as bonus later).
- Add a short “How to Play” screen that explains the one-button spin control and limb loss.
- Keep the code clean, commented, and modular so levels and stats are easy to tweak.
- Target 60 FPS, responsive controls, and satisfying bounce feedback.

Start by scaffolding the project, implementing the core robot physics + one-button spin control + limb destruction, then a single complete level with AI, then the chip/upgrade system, then more levels and menus.

Make the recreation as faithful as possible to the 2007 original’s feel, humor, and destruction loop.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
